newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr recovery soothes debt markets at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr recovery soothes debt markets at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 91.99 (PREV 92.10) 90-DAYS 8.43 (PREV 8.33)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.30 PCT (PREV 8.05) US 5-YR 6.02 (PREV 6.08)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 766.25 (PREV 757.79) Reuters NZ MCI -59 vs -66
* NZ yields claw back some ground at close after poor start
* Bills find good buying interest in afternoon trade
* Government T-bill tender extremely well supported
New Zealand bill rates clawed back some ground lost during Tuesday's session but the day's poor start proved too much of a hurdle to overcome completely.

The 90-day bank bills, which opened at 8.54 percent and traded as high as 8.60 percent, ended near their lows at 8.43 percent. At that level rates were still 10 basis points higher than Monday's 8.33 percent close.
Dealers said good buying interest emerged in early afternoon trade as the New Zealand dollar pushed back up above US$0.6450. It ended at US$0.6459/66 from its 0.6420/27 open.
The currency's Trade-Weighted Index finished at 64.64 from its 64.30 open and 64.68 close on Monday.

A Wellington bill dealer said the market took heart from a contraction in the Monetary Conditions Index to around 45 basis points easier than the central bank's desired level. The market knew it could take the MCI out to -70, so became bid around -45, the dealer said.
"There was a lot of buying seen this afternoon. They seem theoretically good levels, but people are still nervous about the currency.
"But we think given the current mix of conditions, with interest rates so high and the currency so low, the Reserve Bank maybe is concerned about the effect on domestic growth.
"Maybe you don't have to follow the two-for-one trade off as stringently as we did before when 90-day rates were low and the currency was high."
The Reserve Bank equates the impact on future inflation of a 100 basis point move in 90-day interest rates with an offsetting two percentage point move in the TWI.

Meanwhile, dealers said a government tender of NZ$200 million Treasury bills was very well supported given that the TWI had not shown any real improvement by 11.30 a.m. when bids closed. The tender, which attracted $848 million worth of bids, saw the 98-day T-bill yield an average 8.263 percent.

The long bonds managed a rally in response to the good fortunes of U.S. Treasuries. The 11/06 maturity ended the day three pips lower in yield at 6.82 percent in response to a five basis point rally in the U.S. 10-year bond.
